question: In EU Pilot EUP(2021)10037, the Commission clarified that in so-called investor selection procedures, the total value of the construction projects in question matters and that, as a result, the contracts awarded by Deutsche Bahn AG to private investors for the construction of new railway station buildings in Ingolstadt, Paderborn and Hamburg-Altona had to be put out to tender in the Official Journal of the EU.
This, however, has not been done in two of the three cases, and only incorrectly so in the case of Hamburg-Altona as, among other things, it is claimed that the tender is merely voluntary. 1.
Have the German authorities confirmed to the Commission that they now share this legal opinion?
If not, how does the Commission plan to proceed?
If so, what conditions will the Commission impose for the aforementioned construction projects that are yet to commence in Hamburg-Altona and Ingolstadt?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.10.2025) Although German authorities should have tendered out the contracts for building the three specific stations mentioned by the Honourable Member, there was not enough evidence to conclude a systematic breach of EU public procurement rules. Hence, this led to the closure of the EU-Pilot/pre-infringement dialogue mentioned by the Honourable Member.

This is irrespective of whether the German authorities share the same legal assessment of the conditions under which the procurement of all the respective stations falls under public procurement law. In case of alleged breach of EU rules on public procurement in specific procedures, interested parties can approach review bodies and national courts.
In these cases, it is up to the national courts to apply and enforce citizens' rights under EU law.
